stem:
Aisha sketches the stars at 7 p.m. in May. In November she looks again at 7 p.m. The night sky at that same clock time has changed. On one May night she also compares the 7 p.m. sky with the sky at 1 a.m. She is deciding whether Earth’s rotation on its axis or Earth’s revolution around the Sun explains the month-to-month change at the same clock time.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The change from May’s 7 p.m. sky to November’s 7 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s revolution around the Sun.
The change from May’s 7 p.m. sky to November’s 7 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s rotation on its axis.
Rotation is Earth moving around the Sun; revolution is Earth turning on its own axis.
The entire difference between May’s 7 p.m. sky and May’s 1 a.m. sky is caused only by Earth’s revolution around the Sun.

teacher.key_rationale: Month-to-month change in the night sky at a fixed clock time comes from Earth’s revolution around the Sun. Rotation turns Earth on its axis and explains night-to-dawn changes at one place, not the seasonal sky shift at the same clock time.
